subject: DPA intake and SCC module recommendation for EU launch
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: André Kovács <andre.kovacs@fintechly.com>, legal@fintechly.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: DPA intake and SCC module recommendation for EU launch

Hi André / Fintechly legal team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Redwood's role: we expect to act as Data Processor for payments and transaction metadata; Fintechly will be Controller for customer PII. Please confirm if that matches your internal mapping.
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type I completed (Aug 2026). SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress with expected issuance in March 2027. I included the SOC 2 status in the attached DPA template for transparency.
- GDPR / SCC: based on the controller/processor split discussed, our recommendation is to use the Controller->Processor SCC module (Module 2 under the new SCC set). We'll attach a short proposal explaining why Module 2 is the right fit and where the Annex will need to be customized (subprocessors, data categories, retention).
- Data residency: you asked about EU data residency. We can offer Frankfurt (eu-central-1) tenancy for production keys and logging; design details in the SCC proposal.
- Vendor security questionnaire: happy to start a SIG-lite or your questionnaire. If you send the form we’ll aim to return answers within 3 business days.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm controller/processor mapping (one-line reply).
2) If you can share the completed DPA intake form (attached is our intake and a DPA template), we’ll populate the SCC Annex draft.
3) If you want, schedule a 30-min follow-up with legal/ops to walk the SCC Annex — propose Wed Jan 13 10:00 AM CET / 01:00 AM PST (flexible).

Attachments: redwood_dpa_template_v3.pdf (DPA + Annex checklist), scc-module-proposal.pdf (short rationale)

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers up front:
- Controller/Processor: confirmed — Fintechly will be Controller; Redwood will be Processor.
- I attached our DPA intake (filled) for the items you requested.
- Subprocessors: we need a list (by role) of Redwood subprocessors, and we will require notification prior to onboarding any new subprocessors that will touch production PII.
- Data residency: Frankfurt tenancy is a showstopper for our production; please confirm mechanisms for key separation and logging retention in that region.

Also, we run a short in-house security questionnaire; I’ve cc'd Lars from Privacy Advisors who is supporting us on data transfer decisions. Lars — feel free to flag anything obvious.

André —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the intake. A few clarifications and commitments from our side: 

- Subprocessors: we will provide a current roster (roles and company names) in the SCC Annex draft. Operationally, Redwood uses a small set of subprocessors for monitoring and metrics (e.g., observability provider) and a managed cloud provider for compute/storage; we will list them and include the contractual notification clause you requested.
- Data residency / key separation: for Frankfurt tenancy we can offer customer-isolated keys via KMS per-tenant, and logs can be retained on EU-only storage for the agreed retention window. I’ve noted this in the SCC proposal attachment.
- SCC module: we recommend Module 2 (Controller -> Processor). Lars, from a transfer-risk perspective do you see any reason to prefer a different module given Fintechly’s cross-border flows?
- SOC 2 timeline: SOC 2 Type II is expected March 2027. If you need interim evidence now we can provide Type I report and our control mapping spreadsheet; we can also arrange a readout demo with our security lead.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to convert the filled DPA intake into a draft DPA + SCC Annex (we’ll push a redlined PDF). Target: Jan 14 EOD.
- Fintechly to confirm whether you want a vendor questionnaire (SIG-lite) returned before the annex review; if yes, send the doc and we’ll commit to 3 business days.
- Schedule 30-min annex walk-through with legal + security.

I’ll start the draft and loop in Legal (Jordan) if we hit contract-level questions.

Regards,
Rachel
